summary: Review social security entitlements, claims, and grievance routes with practical rights-based tools. Explore the five-day training outline.
lede: Rights-based social security training helps social protection practitioners assess benefit entitlements, access barriers, and administrative decisions. Participants practise mapping entitlement pathways, reviewing eligibility and claim records, and identifying accessible grievance routes. They also develop coverage evidence and accountability tools to report findings and prioritize practical actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work directly with social security entitlements, benefit administration, claims, and accountability. It suits intermediate-level practitioners who need to connect rights commitments to operational decisions and evidence.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with social protection, social insurance, benefit administration, human rights, or related policy work is recommended. No legal qualification or coding/programming is required.
